headline: Very Strong El Nino -- RONI +1.97 degC (ASO 2026; legacy ONI +2.46), power index 84/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: Established El Nino episode: 5 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC (NOAA requires 5).

mjo.note: CPC's newest pentad is 20 days old (25 Oct), too old to say where the active phase is now.

notes: 4 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

alerts.title: Formal El Nino episode criteria met
alerts.detail: 5 consecutive overlapping seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC, from AMJ 2026. NOAA's five-season rule is satisfied.

alerts.title: Projected to peak in very strong territory
alerts.detail: Ensemble peak +2.28 degC at NDJ 2026, 94% probability of exceeding +2.0 degC.

alerts.title: RONI at or above +2.0 degC - Very strong El Nino
alerts.detail: ASO 2026 RONI is +1.97 degC, which CPC prints as +2.0: Very Strong El Nino conditions this season. An event's category is set by its peak, which is still ahead of it while it is building.

alerts.title: Heat content still rising during an active event
alerts.detail: WWV is +0.052 x10^14 m3 per month and still climbing while the surface anomaly is already large. Events normally begin discharging by this stage; continued recharge means the event has not yet spent its fuel.

alerts.title: Third-warmest ASO or better
alerts.detail: Rank 2 of 77 for this calendar season on RONI.

alerts.title: Ocean and atmosphere are coupled
alerts.detail: Composite atmospheric index +1.83 sigma, with 90% of indicators in agreement.

alerts.title: Warm water volume in the top five on record
alerts.detail: Rank 3 of 561 months at +3.16 x10^14 m3.

alerts.title: Still intensifying
alerts.detail: RONI rose +0.28 degC from the previous season (intensifying rapidly).

alerts.title: Invest 95P: high potential for a tropical cyclone within 24 h
alerts.detail: JTWC's advisory of 14 Nov 2026 13:00 UTC places it near 9.2S 157.1W and rates the potential for a significant tropical cyclone within 24 hours high.

alerts.title: East and central Pacific: 2.6x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 359 units of accumulated cyclone energy against 138 for a normal season by 14 November. 25 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 11 major.

alerts.title: Repeated westerly wind forcing over the warm pool
alerts.detail: 6 months in the last year averaged strongly westerly at 850 hPa in the western Pacific, which is how downwelling Kelvin waves get launched.

alerts.title: Legacy ONI and official RONI diverging
alerts.detail: ONI +2.46 against RONI +1.97, a gap of +0.49 degC. That much of the raw anomaly is the whole tropical ocean running warm rather than the Pacific, which is why CPC has classified on RONI since February 2026.

alerts.title: Atlantic: 0.16x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 20 units against 119 normal by 14 November. A suppressed basin is the expected signature of El Nino in the Atlantic, and it is not a reason to relax: 1992 was a quiet season and it produced Andrew.

alerts.title: Westerly wind event under way: east region, 180-150W, 5S-5N
alerts.detail: 42.5 days above +2 m/s since 2026-10-01 06Z in CCMP's near-real-time winds to 2026-11-12, peaking at +10.5 m/s on 2026-11-07; longer than any of the 351 events in Harrison and Vecchi's 1986-1995 list (at most 32.5 days): a sustained westerly anomaly more than a burst. Equatorial westerly anomalies force downwelling Kelvin waves east.

outlook.label: Invest 95P
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 95P) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 9.0S 157.8W IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 9.2S 157.1W, APPROXIMATELY 853 NM EAST- NORTHEAST OF PAGO PAGO. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS A CONSOLIDATING LOW LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) WITH PERSISTENT DEEP CONVECTION BUILDING OVER THE CENTER WITH A FORMATIVE RAINBAND TO THE NORTHERN FLANK OF THE LLCC. A BULLSEYE 140756Z ASCAT METOP-B 25KM PASS SHOWS A SWATH OF 20-25 KNOT WINDS THROUGHOUT THE SOUTHERN SEMICIRCLE. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH LOW VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF 10-15 KNOTS, STRONG RADIAL OUTFLOW ALOFT DUE TO A POINT SOURCE DIRECTLY OVERHEAD, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SST) OF 29-30C. GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS ARE IN GOOD AGREEMENT 95P WILL FURTHER CONSOLIDATE WHILE REMAINING QUASI-STATIONARY OVER THE NEXT 12 TO 24 HOURS BEFORE TRACKING WEST-SOUTHWESTWARD THEREAFTER. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 28 TO 33 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1004 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS UPGRADED TO HIGH. SEE REF A (WTPS21 PGTW 141300) FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

outlook.label: Invest 92B
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 92B) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 8.3N 87.6E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 9.1N 86.2E, APPROXIMATELY 416 NM SOUTHWEST OF PORT BLAIR. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS INVEST 92B WITH A BROAD LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC) AND FLARING CONVECTION THROUGHOUT THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS INDICATES A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH LOW (10-15 KTS) VERTICAL WIND SHEAR, MODERATE RADIAL OUTFLOW ALOFT, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (29-30C). GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS DEPICT GRADUAL DEVELOPMENT OVER THE NEXT 48 HOURS AS THE SYSTEM TRANSITS NORTHWESTWARD. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1008 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS LOW.

outlook.label: Invest 96S
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 96S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 2.1S 86.7E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 1.2S 91.0E, APPROXIMATELY 777 NM SOUTH-SOUTHWEST OF PORT BLAIR. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS INVEST 96S EMBEDDED WITHIN A SHARP TROUGHING REGION WITH A STRONG WESTERLY WIND BURST ALONG THE EQUATOR JUST TO THE NORTH. A 131232Z WSFM 89 GHZ MICROWAVE IMAGE SHOWED SIGNS OF SOUTHERLY WINDS BEGINNING TO WRAP INTO THE SYSTEM IN THE WESTERN PERIPHERY. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS INDICATES THAT 96S IS IN A MARGINALLY FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MODERATE POLEWARD OUTFLOW ALOFT, MODERATE TO HIGH (20-25 KTS) NORTHEASTERLY SHEAR, AND WARM (29-30 C) SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES. GLOBAL MODELS AGREE ON 96S TRACKING GENERALLY EASTWARD, HOWEVER, THEY DISAGREE ON THE AMOUNT OF DEVELOPMENT. THE ECMWF DETERMINISTIC MODEL HAS STARTED SHOWING QUICK CONSOLIDATION OVER THE NEXT 24 HOURS, WHILE GFS TAKES MUCH LONGER. ADDITIONALLY, VARIOUS ENSEMBLE MODELS SHOW ONLY A HANDFUL OF MEMBERS THAT REACH TROPICAL CYCLONE STRENGTH. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS REMAINS LOW.

stormfury.verdict: No live storm to assess. The seedability criterion fails for every storm regardless, so the count would be zero.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 37 natural eyewall expansions in 13 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 28.0% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.3%, overstating it 6.5-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 25 of 300 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 56 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

atlas.method: Past El Ninos (RONI >= +1.0) minus neutral years (|RONI| < 0.5), per season, per grid cell, since 1979, with each event and each neutral year counted once. Welch's t accompanies every difference and is judged against each season's own 95% point of Student's t. An event under way when the grids were built is left out.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).
cpc_discussion.body:
Compared to last month, El Nino strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0°C, extending farther westward across the eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean [Fig. 1] . The Nino indices increased, reaching +2.5°C in Nino-3.4, +3.6°C in Nino-3, and +4.4°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained significantly above average [Fig. 3] , associated with a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Convection and rainfall remained enhanced from the central to the eastern Pacific, while suppressed conditions persisted over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were consistently negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected the ongoing evolution of El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen before beginning to weaken in early 2027 [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Chances for a historic event exceeding previous El Ninos dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ) are now ~60% for the October-December and November-January periods, remaining at better than even odds. Even with a very strong El Nino, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are higher, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than a 79% chance).
